title: Wolf Creek
full_review:
Coed backpackers are once again the prey of choice in the graphically violent Australian thriller "Wolf Creek" (Dimension).

Inspired by true events and obscene in its disturbing realism, the horror film tells the story of a trio of ill-fated hikers (Cassandra Magrath, Nathan Phillips and Kestie Morassi) who, stranded in a remote region of the Outback, find themselves in a nightmarish ordeal when they are "rescued" by a neighborly bushman (John Jarratt) who turns out to be a sadistic killer.

Eliciting convincing performances from his Aussie cast, director Greg McLean chillingly creates an unsettling sense of isolation, building suspense before detouring into dehumanizing and bloody depravity.

The film contains gratuitous realistic violence and gore, including vile scenes of mutilation and torture, sexual degradation, as well as recurring rough and sexually raw language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
